sections.title: Life cycle and form
sections.text: Common buckwheat is a fast-growing annual, often about 75 cm tall. Its leaves are arrow-shaped and its small white to pinkish flowers grow in clusters.

sections.title: Seeds and food
sections.text: The triangular achenes are hulled and cooked as a pseudocereal, whole or milled into flour. The above-ground parts can contain fagopyrin, associated with photosensitivity; hulled seed is the usual food portion.

sections.title: Difference from Tartary buckwheat
sections.text: Fagopyrum tataricum has more strongly ridged seeds and is often more bitter; both species are cultivated for their seeds.
